upoaa.note: California uses its own Power of Attorney Law (Div. 4.5) and the earlier Uniform Statutory Form Power of Attorney Act (Part 3, §4400), not UPOAA (2006).

uhcda.note: Division 4.7 is titled the 'Health Care Decisions Law' with no uniform-act short title. Whether the ULC counts it as a UHCDA enactment was not verified.

ugcopaa.note: Conservatorship law is Prob. Code §1800 et seq. with no uniform short title. ULC enactment list not checked.

upc.note: California Probate Code is not the UPC (no informal probate). ULC enactment list not checked.

utc.note: California Trust Law (Prob. Code Div. 9) is not titled the UTC. ULC enactment list not checked.

rufadaa.note: Enacted 2016 (AB 691), originally only for decedents and trusts. Agents and conservators added eff. Jan. 1, 2025 (SB 1458).

revised-uaga.note: Chapter repealed and re-added 2007 (eff. Jan. 1, 2008) with the short title 'Uniform Anatomical Gift Act'. The structure (e.g., §7150.40 priority list) follows the 2006 revised act.

localNames: agent under durable power of attorney
agent under Uniform Statutory Form Power of Attorney

assigned.event: Principal executes a written POA containing the §4124 durability language (or uses the Uniform Statutory Form POA, Prob. Code §4400 et seq.)

starts.event: On execution unless the instrument makes it springing (see financial-poa-springing)
starts.note: California's default 'effective on execution' rule for a non-springing POA was inferred from §4030 (springing defined as the exception); the form language in §4401 is not online.

ends.event: Death of principal, except specific authority permitted by statute after death; good-faith acts without knowledge of death still bind
Revocation, removal, resignation, agent's death or incapacity, dissolution/annulment of marriage to principal, terms of POA
Conservator of the estate revokes or amends, but only after an order of the conservatorship court

transitions.event: Conservator of the estate revokes durable POA
conditions: Court in the conservatorship proceeding first orders or authorizes the revocation

patches.diff: California's pre-UPOAA Power of Attorney Law (Prob. Code Div. 4.5, §4000 et seq.) governs. Unlike UPOAA §104, a POA is NOT durable by default: durability requires the §4124 statement. A California conservator of the estate may revoke or amend a durable POA only after the conservatorship court authorizes it (§4206(b)). The Uniform Statutory Form POA Act (§4400 et seq.) is the 1988 uniform form act, not UPOAA.

localNames: attorney-in-fact under nondurable power of attorney

ends.event: Principal loses capacity to contract (not overridable by the instrument)
Death of principal

patches.diff: Consistent with the baseline: incapacity ends a nondurable POA (§4155(a)), and §4155(c) says this cannot be limited by the instrument. Third parties and agents acting in good faith without knowledge of incapacity or death are protected (§4304).

starts.event: Specified future time, event or contingency (e.g., incapacity) occurs; if the POA designates a person to make the determination, when that person signs a written declaration under penalty of perjury

transitions.event: Designated person executes written declaration under penalty of perjury that the contingency occurred
conditions: Third persons may rely on the declaration whether or not the contingency actually occurred

patches.diff: California expressly lets the principal name a person whose penalty-of-perjury declaration conclusively triggers a springing POA, with third-party reliance protection (§4129; statutory-form equivalent §4405). §4129(d) says this is not the only method. UPOAA §109 instead uses a person designated in the POA or, failing that, a physician/psychologist or other authority.

localNames: agent under power of attorney for health care
agent under advance health care directive

assigned.event: Adult having capacity executes a power of attorney for health care (Health Care Decisions Law, Prob. Code §4600 et seq.)

starts.event: Unless the POA provides otherwise, on a determination that the principal lacks capacity, made by the primary physician unless the directive specifies otherwise

ends.event: Determination that the principal has recovered capacity (authority ceases; can resume on a new determination)
Revocation by signed writing or by personally informing the supervising provider
Dissolution or annulment of marriage to the agent
Post-death decisions end once anatomical gift, autopsy, remains disposition and records release are completed
ends.note: §4683(b) allows these post-death decisions; the statute does not state a separate end point.

transitions.event: Patient orally designates a surrogate under §4711, who outranks the agent for that treatment/stay or 60 days, whichever is shorter
conditions: Designation does not revoke the agent unless the patient complies with §4695(a)

transitions.event: Principal dies: agent may make anatomical gift, authorize autopsy, direct disposition of remains, release records
conditions: Subject to limitations in the power of attorney

patches.diff: Similar to UHCDA §2(c) (effective on incapacity; primary physician determines). California-specific points: the agent's authority continues after death for anatomical gifts, autopsy and disposition of remains (§4683(b)), and a health-care agent ranks first to control disposition of remains (H&S §7100(a)(1)). A surrogate the patient designates orally under §4711 temporarily outranks the agent.

assigned.event: Patient lacks capacity with no §4711 surrogate, agent or conservator; the health care provider or facility designee picks an adult who has shown special care and concern

starts.event: Determination of incapacity by primary physician and selection by provider

ends.event: Patient recovers capacity (determination by primary physician)
Patient disqualifies the person
ends.note: §4712(b) cross-references §4715 for exceptions; the retrieved §4715 text concerns disqualification by the patient.

transitions.event: Provider selects surrogate from spouse/domestic partner, adult child, parent, adult sibling, adult grandchild, adult relative or close friend
conditions: Candidate is reasonably available and willing

patches.diff: Unlike UHCDA §5's fixed priority list, California's §4712(b) (added 2023 by AB 2338) lists eligible classes but lets the provider choose among them, based on who has shown special care and concern. It is not a strict descending order. A surrogate the patient designates orally under §4711 is valid for up to 60 days.

assigned.event: Court appoints conservator of the person for an adult unable to provide for personal needs (clear and convincing evidence)

starts.event: Oath taken, bond filed if required, and letters issued; appointment not effective until letters issue

ends.event: Death of conservatee (subject to wind-up duties and continuing court jurisdiction over accounts)
Court order terminating conservatorship

transitions.event: Temporary conservator appointed pending hearing
Court adjudicates conservatee lacks capacity for health care decisions; conservator gains exclusive health care authority
Conservatee dies; conservator may pay last-illness and disposition expenses, then accounts

patches.diff: In California the adult court-appointed 'guardian' is called a conservator (Prob. Code §1800 et seq.). Letters are what make the appointment effective (§2310). A conservator of the person ranks 7th for disposition of remains (H&S §7100(a)(7)).

assigned.event: Court appoints conservator of the estate for person substantially unable to manage finances or resist fraud or undue influence

starts.event: Letters issue after oath and bond

ends.event: Death of conservatee; custody duty continues until estate delivered to personal representative
Court termination order

transitions.event: Conservatee dies: powers limited to custody and conservation pending delivery to personal representative
If remaining estate is within the §13100 limit, conservator may petition to liquidate and transfer under Division 8
Conservator obtains court order to revoke or modify principal's durable POA

patches.diff: The baseline conservator lane holds. California adds post-death custody duties (§2467), a streamlined path to liquidate small estates (§2631(b)), and a court-order requirement before a conservator can revoke a durable POA (§4206(b)). Conservators can also reach digital assets after a noticed hearing (§879.3, eff. 2025).

assigned.event: Named in will; petition for probate filed any time after death (named executor who waits more than 30 days after knowledge may be held to have waived)

starts.event: Letters issue after oath (appointment not effective until letters)

ends.event: Court order of discharge after final distribution and receipts

transitions.event: Before letters, named executor may pay funeral expenses and take necessary measures to preserve the estate
Named executor fails to petition within 30 days after knowledge of death and nomination without good cause
conditions: Court may hold right to appointment waived

patches.diff: Like the UPC, no power to administer exists until letters issue, but California has no UPC informal probate. §8000 allows a petition 'at any time' after death, with no UPC §3-108-style 3-year limit. A named executor has a 30-day waiver risk (§8001) and limited powers before appointment (§8400(b)).

assigned.event: Court appoints by statutory priority (spouse/domestic partner, children, ... public administrator, creditors)

ends.event: Discharge after final distribution

transitions.event: Court appoints special administrator when circumstances require immediate appointment
conditions: Powers limited to preservation or as the order specifies

patches.diff: California's priority list (§8461) includes a domestic partner, a conservator of the estate who has filed a first account, and the public administrator. The special administrator (§8540) serves the role of the UPC special administrator.

localNames: successor of the decedent (Prob. Code §13100 affiant/declarant)

assigned.event: Successor of decedent signs affidavit or declaration under penalty of perjury

starts.event: 40 days have elapsed since death, no administration pending (or PR consents), and gross California real and personal property (excluding §13050 property) is within the cap for the date of death

ends.event: Property collected/transferred; affiant remains answerable to a later-appointed personal representative or persons with superior right

transitions.event: Affidavit delivered to holder with certified death certificate and the Judicial Council list of adjusted amounts
conditions: On or after Apr. 1, 2022 and before Apr. 1, 2025: $184,500

transitions.event: Real property affidavit filed no sooner than 6 months after death (separate cap: $69,625 for deaths on/after Apr. 1, 2025)

patches.diff: California waits 40 days (UPC §3-1201: 30 days). The cap is tied to the date of death and adjusted every three years by the Judicial Council under §890. §13100's text still says $166,250, but §13101(g) applies the published adjusted amount for deaths on or after Apr. 1, 2022: $208,850 for deaths on or after Apr. 1, 2025. Revocable-trust assets, joint tenancy and some vehicles are excluded (§13050).

assigned.event: Named in trust instrument, or vacancy filled per instrument, by trust company with beneficiary agreement, or by court

starts.event: Per trust instrument (commonly settlor-trustee's incapacity or death); when no holder of the revocation power is competent, trustee must give beneficiaries notice and trust copy within 60 days

ends.event: Trust terms, resignation/removal, or completion of distribution

transitions.event: Settlor dies and trust becomes irrevocable: successor trustee serves §16061.7 notification within 60 days (120-day contest warning)
Last holder of revocation power becomes incompetent (method in instrument or judicial determination); duties shift to beneficiaries and 60-day notice

patches.diff: California is not a UTC state. §16061.7 requires a 60-day notice on the settlor's death that starts a 120-day contest period (compare UTC §813 and §604). §15800(b) adds duties when the last person who can revoke becomes incompetent. An attorney-in-fact cannot modify or revoke a trust unless the trust expressly allows it (§15401(c)).

assigned.event: User names designated recipient via a custodian's online tool

patches.diff: Same as RUFADAA §4: an online-tool direction that can be modified overrides a contrary will, trust or POA (§873(a)).

starts.event: Fiduciary gives custodian written request, death certificate (decedent), letters or §13101 small-estate affidavit or court order; content requires user consent or court direction

ends.event: Fiduciary authority ends (e.g., discharge); custodian must comply within 60 days of a complete request

transitions.event: Custodian discloses content of deceased user's communications to PR
conditions: Deceased user consented or court directs
Custodian may request court findings under §876(e)(3)

transitions.event: Agent under POA obtains catalogue/other assets (general or specific authority) or content (express authority)
conditions: Applies to POAs executed before, on, or after Jan. 1, 2025

transitions.event: Court grants conservator access to catalogue/non-content digital assets after noticed hearing
Fiduciary or §13101 affiant requests account termination
conditions: Conservator needs court order authorizing termination

patches.diff: California enacted RUFADAA in 2016 (AB 691) for decedents and trusts only. Agents under POAs and conservators were added effective Jan. 1, 2025 (SB 1458; §§879.1–879.3). No court order is required in every case: a personal representative gets content if the user consented or a court directs (§876), though a custodian may ask for court findings. A §13101 small-estate affiant counts as a personal representative's credential (§§876(c), 877(c)).

localNames: agent under power of attorney for health care (anatomical gift)

assigned.event: POA for health care or other record expressly permits agent to make anatomical gift

starts.event: Lifetime (if record permits) or at death as first-priority class member

patches.diff: Follows Revised UAGA §9's priority list (H&S §7150.40), adding domestic partners to the spouse class. California requires a 12-hour search before a coroner, medical examiner or hospital administrator may consent (§7150.40(a)(10)(B)). A donor's refusal, or the donor's membership in a religion that relies on prayer for healing, bars gifts by others (§7150.30).

patches.name: Person with right to control disposition of remains
localNames: agent under power of attorney for health care with right and duty of disposition
patches.summary: The person who controls disposition of remains, the location and conditions of interment, and funeral arrangements, and who bears the duty and liability for disposition costs.

assigned.event: Principal names an agent in a power of attorney for health care (first priority); otherwise the right vests by statutory order. The decedent may also leave binding written directions (§7100.1)

ends.event: Right relinquished to the next class if the holder fails to act or delegate within 7 days (10 days for a surviving spouse) or cannot be found
Disposition completed
ends.note: No explicit statutory end point; inferred from the nature of the right.

transitions.event: Death: right vests in first available class
conditions: Order: (1) health care agent; (2) competent surviving spouse; (3) majority of adult children; (4) parents; (5) majority of adult siblings; (6) next degree of kinship; (7) conservator of person; (8) conservator of estate; (9) public administrator (sufficient assets)

transitions.event: Holder fails to act/delegate within 7 days (10 days for spouse) or cannot be found; right passes to next class
Co-equal holders fail to agree within 7 days; court petition decides and sets alternates
Holder charged with murder or voluntary manslaughter of decedent; right passes (restored if charges dropped/acquitted)

patches.diff: New role. California has no separate 'designated agent for disposition' form. The agent is the health care agent under Prob. Code §4683(b)(3), who ranks first under H&S §7100(a)(1). Conservators rank after all kin.
